lines.text: Clocks went back. An extra hour, and you still look like you need three.
Clocks went back. Dark by five now. You'll take that personally.
Clocks went back. Darker evenings. Finally, lighting that flatters you.
Clocks went back. Your phone did all the work. You just slept through it.
Clocks went back. That hour went to nothing in particular. Classic you.
Clocks went back. Same outfit, one more hour of it. Lucky everyone.
Clocks went back. You'll still say you didn't get a weekend.
The clocks went back. You had a whole extra hour and still look like this.
Clocks went back. You'll mention it to everyone like you did it yourself.
Clocks went back. What did you do with the extra hour? Exactly.
Notice: the extra hour is non-refundable. You've already used it.
Clocks went back. Dark by five, so nobody will see that outfit anyway.
Clocks went forward. Your phone handled it. Your face didn't.
Clocks went forward. You'll yawn all day like it's a personality.
Clocks went forward. Lighter evenings are coming, and you'll still stay in.
Clocks went forward. I changed in a second. You'll need until Wednesday.
Clocks went forward. You'll say 'it's really only seven' all day. It isn't.
Clocks went forward. You lost an hour you'd have wasted anyway.
Clocks went forward. You'll need a second coffee just to look like this.
Clocks went forward. Daylight till late now, so everyone gets a better look at you.
Clocks went forward. One hour less of today. Not much you'll miss.
Clocks went forward. Lost: one hour. Found: those bags under your eyes.
Clocks forward. One hour gone. None of it was your best.
Clocks went forward. Your lost hour isn't coming back. Neither is your Sunday.
Longest day of the year. Plenty of time to do the one thing you'll do.
Longest day of the year. The sun's working overtime. You could try a little.
Longest day of the year. No excuses about the dark today. You'll find others.
Longest day of the year. Maximum daylight on that outfit. Bold.
Longest day of the year. Lots of light, and you'll still pick the dim corner.
Longest day of the year. All that light, and you'll still squint at me.
Longest day of the year. Bad day to look tired. Lots of witnesses.
Longest day of the year. More daylight to see you in. Brave of the sun.
Longest day of the year. You'll still nap through some of it.
Today: maximum daylight. Your plans: still minimal.
Midsummer. Some countries dance around a maypole all night. You'll check the weather.
Longest day of the year. Daylight on you until late. I'm not sure that's a gift.
Shortest day of the year. Less light on that face. A small mercy.
Shortest day of the year. Finally, one that matches your attention span.
Shortest day of the year. You'll still manage to look tired for all of it.
Shortest day of the year. Not much of it, so don't spend it frowning at me.
Shortest day of the year. Your vitamin D and your enthusiasm, both at record lows.
Shortest day of the year. You'll call it 'a long day' anyway.
Shortest day of the year. The dark comes early. Your excuses came earlier.
Shortest day of the year. From tomorrow it gets lighter. You won't.
Shortest day of the year. The sun's barely trying. Finally, someone at your level.
Shortest day of the year. In candlelight, honestly, you look great.
Shortest day of the year. The sun's doing the bare minimum. Your role model.
Shortest day of the year. Less daylight, fewer people seeing you in it. Everybody wins.
Slow and careful. Your usual pace, basically.
Short, flat-footed steps. Not your best look. Wear it anyway.
There's no dignified way to cross ice. You never had much to lose.
Elegance is off today. Nobody will notice the difference.
Grab every railing. Clingy is a good look on you today.
Small steps today. You've had plenty of practice not getting far.
Everyone looks silly on ice. For once you'll blend in.
Your penguin walk is ready. Nobody's judging. I'm judging a little.
Go slowly. Nobody was expecting you early anyway.
Shuffling suits you. I've always thought so.
Glamour can wait. It's been waiting a while.
Today the slowest walker out there is the smartest. Your one chance.
Not that anyone's looking at this hour. Lucky.
Bit late to worry how it looks. It was a bit late this morning too.
Rest of the night sorted. Shame about tomorrow's face.
It'll still be fine at two a.m. That's not a dare.
The outfit's ready for the rest of the night. Your eyes say otherwise.
At this hour, the outfit looks better rested than you.
Nothing left to dress for tonight. Not that you ever do.
The weather's done for today. You could take the hint.
Nobody's going to see it now. Probably for the best.
Good news: nothing changes tonight. That includes you.
I'll be here all night, looking good. One of us has to.
Night forecast: you, here, later than planned. I'm never wrong.
Yes, long pants. Your legs have had their moment. It was brief.
Nobody was asking to see your knees anyway.
You want shorts. You've wanted a lot of things.
Long pants. Your legs will thank me. You won't, but they will.
Your knees aren't as young as you think. Long pants.
Shorts are tempting, I know. Nobody will miss them.
The sun's out and you want shorts. Adorable. The cold front doesn't care.
You'll look like the only one who read the forecast. Because you were.
Long pants in sunshine. Tragic for your legs. Great for everyone else.
Your knees have requested long pants. Please don't ignore them again.
Long pants now, and later you get to say 'told you'. Except I said it.
I'm not saying your legs are the problem. The cold front is. Mostly.
Shade's free. Even you can afford it.
Sitting in the shade isn't lazy today. Enjoy the alibi.
Drink before you're thirsty. You've never planned ahead, so start now.
Nobody looks good red and sweaty. You'd be starting from behind anyway.
Sweat isn't a good look. You don't need the extra help.
Keep the bottle with you. It's the one accessory that suits you.
The shade is where the smart people are. Go anyway.
Water, not heroics. You were never the heroic type.
Stay out of the midday sun. A tan won't fix much.
Today the shade is the cool kids' table. They'll let you sit there. Just today.
Water first, opinions later. You have a lot of opinions.
Shade and water. For once, the advice is easier than you are.
The umbrella won't save your hair. Nothing has so far.
You'll text someone 'did you hear that?' They did. Everyone did.
Thunder for a while. Finally something louder than your opinions.
You'll stand at the window looking dramatic. It doesn't suit you.
A dark, moody sky. Finally an atmosphere that matches you.
You'll say 'that was close' about thunder miles away.
The sky's moody today. You can stop competing.
You'll unplug the router and feel like a survivalist.
That umbrella makes you look prepared. Enjoy it, it's rare.
If the lights flicker, I'll still be here. You'll still look like that.
The storm's getting more attention than you've had all year.
You'll film the lightning and get a gray rectangle. I'm a gray rectangle. You could have filmed me.
World Bicycle Day. You know what Lycra does to you. Please don't.
World Bicycle Day. Everyone on two wheels looks smug. You'd look smug and slow.
World Bicycle Day. Wherever your bike is, your fitness is right next to it.
World Bicycle Day. Helmet hair is a risk you can't afford.
World Bicycle Day. Bikes look great in shop windows. On you, less so.
World Bicycle Day. You can still ride one, can't you. It's been a while.
World Bicycle Day. You'll say 'it's like riding a bike' about anything but a bike.
World Bicycle Day. Your helmet still has the price tag on, I bet.
World Bicycle Day. Cyclists will talk about it all day. You'll nod like you own one.
Happy World Bicycle Day. Your legs asked me to say nothing.
World Bicycle Day. Ring a bell at someone. That's as close as you'll get.
World Bicycle Day. The bike's free. The courage, I see, costs extra.
Happy Easter. Your 'Sunday best' is a clean T-shirt, isn't it.
Easter Sunday. Even the bunny has more energy than you this morning.
Happy Easter. Your painted eggs probably look like small accidents.
Happy Easter. A grown adult on an egg hunt. Show some dignity. Or win.
Easter Sunday. Pastel suits nobody. It suits you even less.
Happy Easter. Bunny ears would improve you. Just saying.
Easter Sunday. All those hidden eggs, and still nobody's looking for you.
Happy Easter. Chocolate bunnies are hollow inside. Don't take it personally.
Easter Sunday. Even the eggs got dressed up today. You could try.
Easter Sunday. You're not too old for an egg hunt. You're too slow.
Happy Easter. You're the reason the good chocolate gets hidden higher.
Happy Easter. Of everyone at the egg hunt, only you brought a strategy. And lost.
May the fourth. You think you'd be a Jedi. You'd be an extra.
May the fourth be with you. Somebody has to be.
Star Wars Day. You'd make a great stormtrooper. Lots of effort, nothing hit.
Star Wars Day. Chewbacca's hair looks better than yours. I'm sorry.
Star Wars Day. You'd be a Jedi if it didn't involve training. Or getting up.
Star Wars Day. Your Jedi robe is a bathrobe, and you know it.
Star Wars Day. You'll mention the original trilogy like you were there.
Star Wars Day. You'd last about four minutes in the Rebel Alliance.
Star Wars Day. You'll quote a line wrong and defend it for ten minutes.
Strong with you, the Force is not. Today, or ever.
Star Wars Day. Hairy and grumpy before coffee. Chewbacca, basically.
These aren't the jokes you're looking for. Then again, you're not who I was looking for either.
Happy New Year. Still you. Nobody got an upgrade.
Happy New Year. You look like last night won.
Happy New Year. Fresh start. Same pajamas, probably.
Happy New Year. A whole new year to look tired in.
New Year's Day. Everyone's sharing their year in review. Yours fits on a sticky note.
Happy New Year. You're one year older and it's already showing.
New Year's Day. A new year, and you're starting it on the couch, probably. Traditional.
New Year's Day. Everyone's a 'new me' today. You're sticking with the old one. Bold.
New Year's Day. The gym's full of resolutions. You're not one of them.
Happy New Year. I didn't make a resolution. I didn't need one. Look at me. Now look at you.
Happy New Year. A whole day in, and you haven't changed a thing. Impressive.
New Year's Day. Resolution check: still horizontal? Right on track.
Oktoberfest. Lederhosen are a look. Not your look.
Oktoberfest. The servers carry ten steins at once. You complain about the grocery bags.
Oktoberfest. Even the pretzels are in better shape than you.
Oktoberfest. You'd look great in a beer tent. It's dark in there.
Oktoberfest. You'd be the one asking if they have anything light.
Oktoberfest. The dancing's on the benches. For everyone's sake, stay on the floor.
Oktoberfest. Long wooden tables full of loud strangers. Your idea of hell, isn't it.
Oktoberfest. Everyone's suddenly an expert on German beer. You're no exception.
Oktoberfest. A dirndl would suit you. I'm lying, but it's a festival.
Oktoberfest starts in September. Finally, an event as badly timed as you.
Oktoberfest. Lederhosen show the knees. Think of the people around you.
Oktoberfest. Thousands of people in one tent, and you'd still find a way to stand alone.
Pi Day. Irrational and never-ending, and still easier to follow than you.
Pi Day. Pi goes on forever without repeating itself. Take notes.
Pi Day. Everyone gets to be irrational today. You've had a head start.
Pi Day. The one math holiday, and you'd still need a calculator.
Pi Day. You can't cut a pie evenly. You've never tried. You take the bigger slice.
Pi Day. 3.14. About your score out of ten today.
Pi Day. Circles are perfect. You had to bring the average down somehow.
Pi Day. You'll smile at a math joke so people think you got it.
Pi Day. Some people know a hundred digits. You know where the bakery is.
3.14159… You stopped reading at the dot, didn't you.
Happy Pi Day. If you can't say the digits, say 'pie' confidently. It works for most of your life.
Pi Day. Draw a perfect circle. Go on. I'll wait. Forever, it turns out.
Halloween. You could go without a costume. People would assume.
Halloween. You'll pretend you're not home when the doorbell rings. Same as every day.
Happy Halloween. A sheet with two holes again. Effort, as always.
Halloween. Kids will ask for candy. You'll hand out the kind you don't like.
Halloween. Even the skeletons look more rested than you.
Halloween. The one night you can look like that on purpose.
Halloween. Pumpkins get carved, lit up and admired. You'll get none of those.
Halloween. The scariest thing in here is probably your hair this morning.
Halloween. Trick or treat? With you, it's always the trick.
Halloween. I'm pale, flat and I stare. You're two out of three.
Boo. Sorry, did that work? You look like it worked.
Halloween. Ghosts, witches, vampires. And you, in a costume nobody can name.
Tour de France. Grown men in Lycra, and they still look better than you in jeans.
Tour de France. You'll tell people you follow the Tour. You follow the highlights.
Tour de France. You'd last about one traffic circle.
Tour de France. The riders eat thousands of calories a day. You're keeping up. Minus the riding.
Tour de France. Those calves took years of training. Yours took nothing, and it shows.
Tour de France. A rider crashes, gets up and finishes. You stub a toe and cancel the day.
Tour de France. They shave their legs for speed. What's your excuse?
Tour de France. Those riders are made of legs. You're made of snacks.
Tour de France. You know who's in yellow. You couldn't name a single rider.
Tour de France. The riders get a team car behind them. You'd need a tow truck.
Tour de France. If they gave a jersey for the couch, it'd be yours. In your size, too.
Tour de France. Stage twelve? Fourteen? You've lost count. So has your step counter.
Thanksgiving. The turkey's been dressed with more care than you.
Thanksgiving. Elastic waistband? Good. You planned ahead for once.
Thanksgiving. I'm guessing you're on rolls duty again. They trust you with that much.
Thanksgiving. Your relatives will notice something about you. Out loud.
Thanksgiving. A whole day about gratitude. Your family will do their best with you.
Thanksgiving. Someone at the table will bring up politics. Try not to be that someone.
Thanksgiving. The leftovers will last a week. Your gratitude, about an hour.
Thanksgiving. Football, food and a nap. Your usual Sunday, with an audience.
Happy Thanksgiving. You'll say grace like you've been practicing. You've been eating the stuffing.
Thanksgiving. I'm thankful for one thing: I don't have to sit next to you.
Thanksgiving. The parade has giant balloons. You'll match them by four.
Thanksgiving. My list of things I'm thankful for: me. Feel free to copy it.
Christmas. The tree's better dressed than you, and it's a tree.
Christmas. You'll say 'you shouldn't have'. This time you'll mean it.
Merry Christmas. Santa checked his list twice. Still not sure about you.
Christmas. Your Christmas sweater is ironic. Your waistband isn't.
Christmas. Board game time. Try to lose gracefully. You've had practice.
Christmas. Under the mistletoe, you'll be waiting a while.
Christmas. Only you could look tired after a day off.
Christmas. Someone got you socks again. They've seen how you dress.
Christmas. A gift card again. They know you so well.
Merry Christmas. I didn't get you anything. I'm a screen. What's your excuse?
Christmas. My only wish: you, in better clothes. Not happening.
Christmas. Everyone's glowing, twinkling, sparkling. You're also here.
